data.name: ExampleReadme
data.value:
Example server save: Example-All-Options ========================================
This save shows every server save option filled in once with sensible values. Trebuchet creates it once automatically. To build your own: duplicate it under Server Saves and replace the placeholders. If you delete it, Trebuchet does not create it again.
CHANGE BEFORE THE FIRST START - Admin, server and RCon password (they are set to example values). - Discord webhooks: enter real URLs, in the profile (Discord) and in the action of the starting sequence. Placeholders are ignored or logged as invalid, the server still starts. - Sudo super admins: your Steam ID instead of 76561190000000000. - MULTIHOME is off; 192.168.1.10 is only an example (network configuration > Use for MULTIHOME).
HOW IT WORKS TOGETHER - Restarts: daily at 06:00 and 18:00 (max. 2 per day, at least 2 h uptime), plus mod/server updates and RequiresRestart.txt in the profile or instance folder. - Warnings: 15/5/3/1 minutes before, over RCon (broadcast) and Discord. If nobody is online the server restarts right away. Shortly before the restart the restart message is sent. IMPORTANT: RCon must be on, otherwise no player gets the warnings. A custom stopping sequence would replace the warnings, so it is empty here. - Starting sequence: start the server (main action), wait until online, then 'Message to players' (RCon only, greeting in game) and 'Discord webhook' (formatted announcement, e.g. for a public channel). Replace the webhook URL of the action. The profile webhooks (Discord) get the ready, crash and restart messages separately. - Ready and shutdown messages go to Discord. - Message method broadcast works with every chat mod (popup). totpop shows the popup of Tot ! Chat. - Crash: crashed servers are restarted (max. 3 times in 15 min, then a pause and a Discord message). A server that hangs for more than 300 s is stopped (Kill Crashed Servers). - Backup on every shutdown to %USERPROFILE%\Documents\Conan-Backups\Example-All-Options, 14 daily folders are kept. Afterwards example-after-backup.bat runs (writes script-log.txt). - Voice chat completely off (serverVoiceChat=0 + engine voice off). - Log filters: default list incl. LogOnlineSubsystemFls=Fatal (stops the voice error flood). - Performance: priority 'Above normal', enforced on every refresh. - Additional launch argument -nosound (example for your own arguments).
Note: the notification templates for all servers (crash, online, reasons ...) are at the very bottom of Server Saves and apply to every profile.

data.value: Sends a test message with the selected message method to every running server that uses this save and shows the RCon answer. Check in game whether it arrives. RCon must have been on when the server started.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpOpenGuide
data.value: Open the guide in the browser

data.name: DiscordBotHelpIntro
data.value: This guide takes you through setting up the Discord bot, step by step. Plan about 15 minutes. You need: a Discord account, a Discord server where you are an administrator, and this Trebuchet on the PC that runs your Conan servers. The bot runs inside Trebuchet and only opens an outgoing connection to Discord, no port is opened. Only someone whose Discord user ID is on the list AND who has one of the allowed roles gets access. Try everything with a test server and a test save first: the bot can restart and stop real servers.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep1Title
data.value: Create the bot in the Discord developer portal

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep1Text
data.value: Open https://discord.com/developers/applications in your browser and log in with your Discord account. Click "New Application" at the top right, enter a name (e.g. "Trebuchet Admin"), accept the terms and click "Create". This name is shown on your server later. Click "Bot" in the left menu. You do the next two steps on this page.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep1Hint
data.value: You only need the portal for the setup. Afterwards only to reset the token.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep2Text
data.value: Switch "Public Bot" off. Otherwise anyone can invite the bot to their own server. Under "Privileged Gateway Intents" leave all three switches off ("Presence Intent", "Server Members Intent", "Message Content Intent"). The bot does not need them. Leave "Requires OAuth2 Code Grant" off. Turn on two-factor authentication for the account you use in the developer portal (Discord → Settings → My Account).

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep3Text
data.value: On the "Bot" page click "Reset Token", confirm with your password and copy the token shown. It is a long text with two dots and is shown only once. The token is like a password: whoever has it can log in as your bot. Do not share it in Discord, by e-mail or in screenshots. Keep the token in the clipboard or paste it right away in step 7. Trebuchet stores it encrypted and never shows it again.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep3Hint
data.value: If the token is lost or became known: press "Reset Token" in the portal again. The old token is invalid at once.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep4Title
data.value: Invite the bot to your server

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep4Text
data.value: In the developer portal click "OAuth2" on the left, then "URL Generator". Under "Scopes" tick "bot" and "applications.commands". Under "Bot Permissions" tick only these three: "View Channels", "Send Messages" and "Embed Links". Never "Administrator". Copy the "Generated URL" at the bottom, open it in the browser, choose your server and confirm with "Continue" and "Authorize".

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep4Hint
data.value: The bot then appears in the member list of your server, still offline. It goes online when you start it in Trebuchet.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep5Title
data.value: Turn on developer mode and copy the IDs

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep5Text
data.value: Turn on developer mode in Discord: Settings (cog) → Advanced → Developer Mode. Server ID: right-click the icon of your server → "Copy Server ID". Your user ID: right-click your name (e.g. in the member list) → "Copy User ID". This will be the super admin. Other people who may use the bot: copy their user IDs the same way. Role ID: Server Settings → Roles → right-click the role → "Copy Role ID" (you create the role in the next step). IDs are plain numbers with 17 to 20 digits. You can keep them in a text editor until you enter them in step 7.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep5Hint
data.value: The role "@everyone" is not allowed: every member has it, Trebuchet refuses it.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep6Title
data.value: Create a role and a private channel

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep6Text
data.value: Server Settings → Roles → "Create Role". Name it e.g. "Trebuchet-Admin". The role needs no special permissions. Give the role to everyone who may use the bot, including yourself (click the member → add role). Create a new text channel (e.g. "server-admin") and switch on "Private Channel". Allow only the role "Trebuchet-Admin" and the bot to access it. In this channel the bot needs the permissions "View Channel", "Send Messages" and "Embed Links".

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep6Hint
data.value: Access needs the user ID AND the role. The role alone or the ID alone is not enough, not even for the super admin.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep7Text
data.value: Section "Connection": paste the token and save it, then enter the server ID. After saving, the token is never shown again. Section "Security": enter your user ID as "Super admin" (required, the entry cannot be removed). Enter the role ID under "Allowed roles". Add the IDs of other people under "Allowed users". Section "Servers": tick the servers the bot should manage. The bot shows each server under its "Server name", the first field of its server save (menu "Server Saves"). Change it there if you want another name. A server that is not ticked does not exist for the bot. Click "Save" at the top. If something is invalid or missing, the top shows in red exactly what, and nothing is saved. Optional: enter the ID of a channel as "Audit channel" where the bot reports critical actions and lock-outs.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep7Hint
data.value: Without a token, a server ID, a super admin and at least one role the bot does not start. That is on purpose.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep8Text
data.value: In the section "Security" click "Check security". All items should be green (server reachable, roles exist, no administrator permission, …). For yellow or red read the note and fix it. At the top in the section "Status" click "Start". After a few seconds it says "Connected" and the bot is online on Discord. Optional: switch on "Start with Trebuchet" if the bot should always run.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep9Text
data.value: In the private channel, as super admin, enter the command /bot channel set and confirm with "Confirm". The slash commands only appear once the bot is connected (can take a minute, otherwise reload Discord with Ctrl+R). From then on the bot only answers in this channel and posts one status message with buttons per server there. Releasing the channel again (all channels) is only possible here in the Trebuchet panel, never through Discord.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep9Hint
data.value: The command also works outside the current admin channel, but only for the super admin and only with the role.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep10Text
data.value: The status message always shows the buttons that fit the server: Start (stopped), Restart and Stop (running), Postpone and Release again, and "Check updates". The bot edits this one message right away when something changes and every 5 minutes as a check. Restart and Stop first ask for the warning time (right away, 1, 5, 10, 15, 30 min, 1 h, restart also 2 h), like the dialog in Trebuchet. Then a small window for the reason opens (it may stay empty): submitting it runs the action at once, there is no further question. "Check updates" only asks Steam about mod updates and a new server version and installs nothing. The super admin may use every button without switching anything on. Section "Commands": the switches only decide what the other users may do. On by default are status, postpone, release again and check updates. Off are restart now and stop. Start, update and set channel belong to the super admin alone. You set the limits in the section "Security": wait between commands, how many critical actions are allowed, the longest postponement and the choices (e.g. 15 min, 30 min, 1 h).

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep10Hint
data.value: Switch on only what you really need. The less is on, the less can go wrong.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep11Text
data.value: The status message shows the state per server: green = running, yellow = something is pending, blue = postponed, red = stopped or crashed. When a restart, stop or update is pending, the button "… postpone" appears. A click opens a choice (e.g. 15 min to 6 h), then a small window for the reason (it may stay empty). In game the players get the message that it was postponed. "Release again" ends a postponement. Altogether you can only postpone up to the longest postponement (default 6 h), after that only again after the restart. Everything the bot does or refuses is in the section "Log". Optional: in the "Community log" section you set up a channel of its own for your players (webhook, name, picture). The bot announces planned and automatic restarts and stops there shortly before, says when the server goes down and when it is back online. The audit log can also be written through a webhook under a name and picture of its own.

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep12Text
data.value: "Token refused" or "Connection lost": create the token again in the portal (step 3), enter it here and save. No slash commands in Discord and the panel says "Connected, but the slash commands could not be registered": the bot was invited without "applications.commands". Invite it again with a new link from step 4. "No permission": user ID AND role must match, and so must server and channel. For security the bot does not say what is missing. The exact reason is in the log. The bot does not answer in the channel: is the admin channel set, and do you use the command in that channel? Does the bot have the permissions from step 6 there? "Token already in use" means a bot with the same token already runs in another Trebuchet or in "boulder bot".

data.name: DiscordBotHelpStep12Hint
data.value: If nothing helps: stop the bot, look at "Check security" and open the guide in the browser (button below).

data.name: DiscordBotCommandCheckUpdatesText
data.value: Asks Steam whether mods or the server need an update and reports the result. Nothing is installed.

data.name: DiscordBotServersText
data.value: Choose which servers the bot manages. The bot shows each server under its "Server name" (the first field of its server save), or under the name of the save when that was not changed. A server that is not chosen does not appear in the bot at all, not even for the super admin.

data.name: DiscordBotAuditWebhookText
data.value: Optional. The webhook URL of the audit channel (channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy URL). With it the log is written under the name and with the picture below instead of under the name of the bot, and the channel ID above is not needed. Stored encrypted for your Windows user and never shown again.

data.name: DiscordBotAuditNameText
data.value: Needs the audit webhook. Replaces the name set for the webhook in Discord. Empty: the name of the webhook. Discord does not allow "discord" or "clyde" in a name.

data.name: DiscordBotAuditAvatarText
data.value: A link (https) to an image. Needs the audit webhook. Replaces the picture set for the webhook in Discord. Empty: the picture of the webhook.

data.name: DiscordBotCommunityText
data.value: A log for your players in a channel of its own: it announces a planned restart or stop shortly before it (with the time), says when the server goes down, and when it is back online with how long it was offline. It needs a webhook of its own and runs while the bot runs.

data.name: DiscordBotCommunityEnabledText
data.value: Announces restarts and stops, and that the server is back, in the community channel.

data.name: DiscordBotCommunityWebhookText
data.value: The webhook URL of the community channel (channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy URL). Stored encrypted for your Windows user and never shown again.

data.name: DiscordBotCommunityNameText
data.value: The name the messages appear under, e.g. the name of your server or community. Empty: the name of the webhook. Discord does not allow "discord" or "clyde" in a name.

data.name: DiscordBotCommunityAvatarText
data.value: A link (https) to an image, e.g. the logo of your server. Empty: the picture of the webhook.

data.name: DiscordBotCommunityLeadText
data.value: How long before a planned restart or stop the players are told (1 to 60).

data.name: DiscordBotWebhookNeedsWindows
data.value: The webhook can not be stored on this system.

data.name: DiscordBotWebhookInvalid
data.value: This is not a Discord webhook URL. Nothing was saved.

data.name: DiscordBotWebhookSaveFailed
data.value: The webhook could not be saved, see the log of Trebuchet.

data.name: DiscordBotWebhookRemoveText
data.value: Nothing is written through it any more. If the URL may have leaked, also delete the webhook in Discord.

data.name: DiscordBotIssueInvalidUrl
data.value: The link is not valid (an https link without spaces)

data.name: DiscordBotIssueInvalidName
data.value: The name is not allowed (no "discord" or "clyde" in it, and no token or link)

data.name: DiscordBotCommandCancelText
data.value: Cancels the restart or stop that is counting down. The players are told it does not happen.

data.name: DiscordBotBotIdentity
data.value: Bot takes this name and picture

data.name: DiscordBotBotIdentityText
data.value: The bot account itself takes the name and picture from above: the status message with its buttons and the answers are written by the bot, not by the webhook. Discord allows two changes of the name an hour, and the name counts for every server the bot is on. Empty fields stay as they are. The picture is fetched from this computer.

data.name: DiscordBotIssueBotNameLength
data.value: The name of a bot has 2 to 32 characters

data.name: SettingServerThrallDistanceText
data.value: The greatest distance from a player at which a thrall still counts as relevant (dw.ThrallMaxRelevantDistance in the [SystemSettings] of the Engine.ini of the server). In game units, not metres: a foundation is about 2.6 m wide, roughly 260 units, so 5 foundations are about 1300 and 10 foundations about 2600. 0 writes nothing, the game keeps its own value.

data.name: SettingUpdateRestartCountdownText
data.value: How long the players are warned before a server restarts for a mod or server update (the countdown starts when the update is found). It only applies to saves that have the warning messages switched on and no stopping sequence of their own, and never makes the warning shorter than the longest warning of the save. 0: only the warnings of the save.
